jobs.title: AI Strategist
jobs.jd_full:
Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day.

Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia. Cresta’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu, founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences.

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

About the Role:

As an AI Strategist, you are the embedded AI leader for our customers. You connect what customers are saying in their conversations, what their business needs most, and what Cresta's AI can do, then turn that into a prioritized plan and measurable results. You identify where automation and augmentation will deliver the most value, build the roadmap, and make sure the work ships and pays off.

You will not be building AI Agents from scratch. Our Forward Deployed Engineers and Forward Deployed Product Managers create and deploy them. Your focus is on making deployed AI better: finding the next opportunity, optimizing what is already live, piloting new Cresta capabilities, and proving the business impact. You are analytical, commercially minded, and credible with senior stakeholders in CX, Operations, Product, Sales, and IT. You are technical enough to work closely with FDEs and FDPMs and to give product and engineering a tight feedback loop.

What You'll Do:

AI Strategy and Roadmap

  • Identify automation and augmentation opportunities across the customer's contact center and wider customer experience operation.
  • Prioritize initiatives by expected ROI and build a business case for each one.
  • Build and maintain the customer's enterprise AI roadmap, and keep it current as priorities and Cresta capabilities change.
  • Align stakeholders across CX, Operations, Product, Sales, and IT on priorities, sequencing, and success criteria.

Conversation Intelligence and Business Insights

  • Use conversation data to surface customer friction and emerging trends before they show up in other metrics.
  • Identify operational inefficiencies and the changes that would reduce them.
  • Share Voice of Customer insights with customer leadership and with Cresta product teams.
  • Measure business impact and report it in terms executives care about, such as containment, handle time, conversion, CSAT, and cost to serve.

AI Innovation and Execution

  • Stay current on new Cresta features and bring the relevant ones to customers early.
  • Pilot emerging AI capabilities, define how success will be judged, and decide with the customer whether to scale them.
  • Optimize live AI Agents by analyzing performance, reviewing conversations, and recommending changes to prompts, workflows, and configurations.
  • Coordinate deployments with FDEs, FDPMs, and customer teams, including milestones, timelines, and dependencies.
  • Measure realized value after launch and report it back against the original business case.

What We're Looking For:

  • Experience: 5+ years in technology consulting, strategy, product, analytics, implementation, or customer success roles, ideally with AI or LLM-first products.
  • Strategic and commercial skills: A track record of building roadmaps, prioritizing by ROI, and writing business cases that senior stakeholders approve.
  • Analytical approach: Strong data skills. You are comfortable analyzing conversation or operational data, designing experiments such as A/B tests, and monitoring performance to refine solutions.
  • Technical understanding: Working knowledge of how LLM-based AI agents function, including prompts, tools or function calling, and retrieval-augmented generation. Hands-on experience with an agent project, even a personal one, is a plus. You do not need to write production code, but you can read and reason about system behavior and discuss tradeoffs with engineers.
  • Stakeholder leadership: Experience leading cross-functional work and influencing senior customer stakeholders across CX, Operations, Product, Sales, and IT.
  • Communication: Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills. You can explain a complex finding to an executive in plain language.
  • Execution: Strong project management skills and a bias for action. You turn ambiguity into a plan and follow it through to results.
  • Mindset: Curious, self-driven, and comfortable learning quickly in a fast-moving startup environment. You are passionate about AI, automation, and the future of customer experience.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Bonus Points:

  • Familiarity with customer support and contact center operations, including metrics such as AHT, FCR, containment, and QA
  • Experience with conversation intelligence, speech analytics, or voice-of-customer programs
  • Background in management consulting, product management, or forward deployed roles
  • Experience in a startup or high-growth SaaS environment
  • Comfort with SQL or a BI tool for self-serve analysis

Perks & Benefits:

We offer a comprehensive and people-first benefits package to support you at work and in life:

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with plans to fit you and your family
  • Flexible PTO to take the time you need, when you need it
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents welcoming a new child
  • Retirement savings plan to help you plan for the future
  • Remote work setup budget to help you create a productive home office
  • Monthly wellness and communication stipend to keep you connected and balanced
  • In-office meal program and commuter benefits provided for onsite employees

Compensation at Cresta:

Cresta's approach to compensation is simple: recognize impact, reward excellence, and invest in our people. We offer competitive, location-based pay that reflects the market and what each individual brings to the table.

The posted compensation range represents what we expect to pay for this role in a given location. Final offers are shaped by factors like experience, skills, education, and geography. In addition to base pay, total compensation includes equity and a comprehensive benefits package for you and your family.

jobs.title: Founder's Associate, Strategy Team
jobs.jd_full:
Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners.

We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.

Since launching publicly in September 2023, Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue, with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.

Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue)—the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.

Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.

- Mission-critical problems: We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.

- High bar, low ego: Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.

- Speed over comfort: We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.

- Enduring impact: What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.

Team & Locations

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

Flex Fuels Ambition.

About the Role

This is a new program and the chance to be part of the founding team of the Office of the CEO. We’re creating a small team of high-caliber operators working directly for our Founder & CEO on whatever the company’s highest-priorities are. It is not a rotational program or a fixed analyst lane — scope is set by what the company needs solved, not by a job description. You will be the one to help identify what these opportunities are.

  • Take on the CEO’s highest-priority problems directly — strategic projects, market research and competitive work, financial analysis, and cross-functional execution, often with no existing playbook

  • Identify problems, develop solutions, and execute them; often working on multiple initiatives

  • Build and own the models and analyses that inform major company decisions

  • Collaborate with and move fluidly across various departments as business priorities shift

  • As the early stages of this team grows, you will help recruit, ramp, and manage the associates who join after you

Requirements

  • 3–5 years in top-tier investment banking (TMT/fintech coverage), private equity, management consulting, late-stage venture capital, or a fast-growing startup

  • A track record of outperformance — clear signals you were trusted with more scope, faster, than your peers

  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills: advanced Excel, working knowledge of SQL, and comfort dissecting messy data and building models from scratch

  • Extreme rigor and comfort operating in ambiguity at speed — priorities here change faster than the plan does

  • Demonstrated ability to sustain a high-intensity pace: this role will regularly require ~12-hour days, 5–6 days a week, especially in year one

  • This role is based in Miami or NYC but will involve travel

Nice to Haves

  • Ideal background in math, physics, or another highly quantitative field

  • Understanding of fintech, banking, or financial infrastructure

Compensation

The starting base salary for this role is $200k+ equity. This is a full-time role with benefits. Final compensation is commensurate with candidate experience, work location, and interview performance.

Additional Information

Why Join Us

Build something generational — Capture the full lifecycle of money for ambitious business owners.

Work on real money, real risk — Payments, credit, and banking at serious scale.

Solve hard problems — AI, underwriting, compliance, and global finance from first principles.

True ownership — Small teams, high trust, real accountability.

Founder-level exposure — Direct access to leadership, customers, and investors.

High bar, high taste — Move fast without cutting corners.

Elite peers — People here are builders, not tourists.

Real upside — Meaningful equity if you help build something big.

jobs.title: Director, Commercial Strategy & Operations
jobs.jd_full:
We are looking for a Director of Commercial Strategy & Operations to lead the commercial function inside Revenue Operations. ClickHouse runs on a usage-based pricing model, which makes pricing strategy and commercial system design foundational: the pricing model, packaging, rules, guardrails, discount governance, approval workflows, and marketplace mechanics have to be designed early and built into the system, not retrofit later. The same discipline applies to new products: the commercial infrastructure that makes them sellable has to be built before they ship.

Reporting to the VP, Revenue Operations, you will own the commercial surface of the GTM system end-to-end: the pricing strategy, the packaging, and the rules, automation, and exception review that govern how deals get structured, approved, and closed, and the commercial readiness that makes a new product sellable on day one. The team spans pricing strategy, commercial governance, marketplace operations (CSP transactions, private offers, co-sell), new product commercialization, and commercial systems design. You will partner closely with Product, Finance, Legal, and the CRO on pricing, packaging, and deal strategy.

What You'll Be Doing

  • GTM owner for pricing strategy and packaging. Set the pricing model and packaging architecture in partnership with Product and Finance. Run pricing analysis, model the commercial impact of changes, and lead pricing reviews and pricing changes from analysis through rollout.

  • Own commercial architecture: pricing operationalization, discount governance, approval logic, and the rules and guardrails that govern how deals get structured and closed.

  • Design and operate the commercial review function: rules, approval logic, automated controls, and the exception review process for the deal flow that doesn't fit them. Partner with Sales and Finance on the non-standard cases that genuinely warrant human judgment.

  • Build out Q2C and CPQ automation. Drive the platform roadmap with Revenue Engineering.

  • Own marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: CSP transactions, private offers, co-sell motions, and the operational mechanics behind partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue.

  • Own commercial readiness for new product introduction. Build the commercial infrastructure that makes a new product sellable before it ships: the pricing and packaging, the quoting logic, the discount and approval rules, and the controls that govern how the product gets sold. Program-manage the cross-functional path to launch across Product, Finance, Legal, and Revenue Engineering: define the commercial requirements, drive the build, test the end-to-end flow, and own the go-live readiness so the product is sellable on day one.

  • Hire and develop the Commercial Strategy & Operations team. Design the systems and review logic that let a small team govern an increasing volume of deal flow as the business scales.

  • Partner with Product and Finance on pricing and packaging changes: lead the analysis, design the operational rollout, instrument the rollout in the system, and measure the results

What You Bring Along

  • 10+ years in pricing strategy, commercial operations, revenue strategy, or product-led growth strategy, with at least five years managing a team.

  • Direct experience setting and operationalizing pricing for a usage-based or consumption-based business. You have led at least one significant pricing or packaging change end-to-end: analysis, design, alignment, and rollout.

  • End-to-end Q2C experience. You have owned the quote-to-cash flow for a new product or major SKU from commercial requirements through testing and launch: requirements definition, quoting and approval design, UAT, and go-live. You can hold a cross-functional program to a launch date across Product, Finance, Legal, and Engineering, and you measure readiness by whether the flow works end-to-end, not by whether the pieces exist.

  • Owner-operator mindset. You treat commercial strategy and operations as a system you own end-to-end: you design it, you run it, you fix it when it breaks, and you measure it by what it produces, not by activity.

  • Product-owner instincts. You think about commercial work as infrastructure to design, not a queue to clear. You hire and build for leverage, not headcount.

  • Strong commercial analytics. Comfortable building pricing models, sensitivity analyses, and elasticity views from first principles. SQL fluency required.

  • Familiarity with the operational complexity of usage-based contracts: metering, commits, contract structure, overages, and the rev rec implications.

  • Marketplace fluency. Hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure marketplace operations is strongly preferred.

  • Strong working knowledge of Salesforce CPQ. Comfort designing rules, approval logic, and automated controls, not just configuring tools.

  • Ability to partner with Legal and Finance on contract structure and revenue recognition implications.

  • Excellent judgment on commercial tradeoffs. Comfortable saying no when the deal structure breaks the system, and comfortable advocating for the field when the case is sound.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. Comfortable presenting to executives and engaging with senior customer stakeholders.

  • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, MBA or equivalent experience preferred.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

OpenFn is the digital public good for public service automation & AI orchestration. Our platform automates data exchange and digital workflows so that governments and NGOs can deliver public services more efficiently, achieve interoperability across fragmented systems, and scale critical public services across health, humanitarian, and government programs.

Our team, Open Function Group, the primary steward of this open-source platform, is a lean, fully-remote team of integration specialists, solution architects, and implementation consultants working across 40+ countries.

We are not making marginal improvements to already comfortable lives. We are building the infrastructure that allows governments to function, clinics to operate, and vulnerable populations to access services they depend on.

The role

We need a remote, relationship-driven, commercially-minded Program Manager who is genuinely technically fluent, someone who can speak credibly about our platform, integrations, and data workflows with technical and non-technical stakeholders alike, to keep our existing customers happy, engaged, and growing, and to help us stand up program management as a function for the very first time.

We are hiring our first Program Manager to own and grow relationships with OpenFn’s existing customers as we transition to a subscription model built around packaged product-and-services bundles.

As our first Program Manager in this market, you will own the full portfolio of existing subscription customers and be accountable for their retention, satisfaction, and growth. You will be the trusted advisor customers turn to, the person who makes sure they are getting real value from OpenFn, and the internal owner of the commercial health of each account.

OpenFn is a genuinely technical product: our customers use it to build integrations, move data between systems, and automate complex digital workflows. You do not need to be an engineer, and you will not be doing hands-on implementation work; we have solution architects and implementation consultants for that. But you do need to be technically fluent: able to understand how customers use the platform, hold a credible conversation with their technical teams, spot when something is going wrong, and know when to bring in a specialist. That technical credibility is what will make you a genuine trusted advisor rather than just a point of contact.

Because this is a foundational hire, you will both build and execute. You will not inherit a mature playbook; you will help create it, establishing the processes, cadences, and tooling that a strong program management function depends on, while carrying a live book of business from day one.

Own & grow customer relationships

  • Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for a portfolio of existing subscription customers
  • Build strong, multi-threaded relationships across each customer organization, from day-to-day users through to senior decision-makers
  • Develop and maintain account plans that map each customer’s objectives to the value OpenFn delivers
  • Plan and lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and other regular check-ins

Bring technical fluency to the relationship

  • Develop a strong working understanding of the OpenFn platform and how each of your customers uses it
  • Hold credible, substantive conversations with customers’ technical teams about their integrations, data workflows, and use cases
  • Translate fluently between customers’ technical staff and their non-technical decision-makers
  • Spot technical adoption risks early, and know when to bring in solution architects or implementation consultants

Drive retention & expansion

  • Own gross and net retention for your portfolio, and be accountable for renewals
  • Forecast renewals accurately and manage the end-to-end renewal process
  • Proactively identify at-risk accounts and lead recovery plans before they churn
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to grow accounts, including tier upgrades and cross-sell of additional services
  • Negotiate renewals and expansions in line with our pricing and packaging model

Deliver value & coordinate delivery

  • Ensure a smooth handoff from sales and implementation into ongoing program management
  • Monitor product usage and adoption, and work with customers to close gaps and deepen engagement
  • Act as the voice of the customer internally, channeling feedback to our product and services teams
  • Coordinate with support and implementation teams to meet SLA commitments and deliver project-based work
  • Manage escalations, bringing the right internal people together to resolve issues quickly

Build the program management function

  • Establish the playbooks, cadences, and health-scoring approach that will let program management scale as OpenFn grows

We regard autonomy highly and treat our organisation as a product – we iterate, improve and test things internally to see what works best for everyone.

Our culture:

We believe in creating a safe work environment through humanity, fluidity, safety, transparency and progressiveness. When hiring, we look for culture add rather than culture fit.

Because we are a fully remote team, it’s especially important that we create an environment where our colleagues feel included and connected as humans.

Feeld promotes open-mindedness, inclusion, diversity and kindness, both in the world and among our own workforce.

jobs.jd_full:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Together, we’re changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.

What you will be doing:

Beacon Biosignals is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the roadmap and day-to-day product decisions for our clinician- and site-facing web application, the primary way clinicians, clinical research sites, and trial teams interact with Beacon’s machine-learning-enabled brain health platform. This role reports to the Manager, Web Applications.

In this role, you’ll work within Beacon’s Web Apps team to drive major development milestones for the next generation of Beacon’s web applications for clinicians and clinical sites. You’ll shape product direction in partnership with the team’s manager and turn it into quarterly plans your team can execute against. You’ll be a clear, credible voice for the product with external users and internal stakeholders such as Beacon’s clinical, scientific, regulatory, and commercial teams.

This is a remote position, with a preference for candidates based near Beacon HQ in Boston, or another Beacon hub (e.g., New York City).

What success looks like:

  • Build deep knowledge of clinicians, sleep technicians, site coordinators, investigators, and sponsor teams, and use it to ensure the roadmap reflects their real needs and Beacon’s business goals.
  • Own a single product that serves both diagnostic and clinical trial workflows, identifying where needs overlap and diverge, and make clear, well-reasoned, documented decisions about shared versus specialized functionality.
  • Ensure the web experience is coherent with the wider ecosystem it depends on, including devices, data pipelines, ML models, and other software products. Stay informed about what adjacent teams are building, surface dependencies and conflicts early, and drive convergence so that the pieces work together as a coherent experience for users.
  • Create and evolve quarterly product roadmaps and clear requirements that your team can execute against, that shape the next generation of the web application.
  • Work closely with software engineers, product designers, and data science and machine-learning teams to align on technical specifications and feasibility, and on how model outputs are presented to users.
  • Practice continuous discovery, running formal and informal usability tests and user interviews early and often, with particular attention to the workflows of busy clinicians and site staff.
  • Deliver product requirements and changes through formal design controls in a regulated environment, using contemporary tools (at Beacon, we use Ketryx!).
  • Balance the needs of multiple customer types and internal stakeholders, including clinical operations, regulatory and quality, and commercial teams, and manage external client-facing demos that showcase the product’s current capabilities and roadmap.
  • Communicate project progress, decision-making tradeoffs, and risks with key stakeholders effectively, often, and efficiently.

What you will bring:

  • 5+ years of Product Management experience, including  at least 3 years of experience managing web-based software products.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in business, engineering, or a related field; or equivalent experience.
  • Experience working on highly technical products, such as data platforms, analytics products, or machine-learning-enabled applications.
  • Experience working across engineering, design, and non-technical stakeholders, and balancing competing priorities among them.
  • Experience in healthcare, life sciences, or biotech is strongly preferred, along with the ability to learn clinical context quickly.
  • Experience developing regulated software (e.g., software as a medical device or clinical trial systems) under design control (e.g. IEC 62304) is strongly preferred.
  • Experience designing for clinicians, clinical sites, or other expert-users is a plus.
  • Comfort and enthusiasm for using modern tools to speed up product work, such as AI-assisted drafting, analysis, and rapid prototyping. We care more about how you’ve used them than which ones.

The salary range for this role is $160,000 – $183,000. Salary ranges are determined using current market compensation data for this role and adjusted based on experience, skills, and location. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes equity, PTO and other benefits.

At Beacon, we’ve found that cultural and scientific impact is driven most by those that lead by example. As such, we’re always seeking new contributors whose work demonstrates an avid curiosity, a bias towards simplicity, an eye for composability, a self-service mindset, and - most of all - a deep empathy towards colleagues, stakeholders, users, and patients. We believe a diverse team builds more robust systems and achieves higher impact.
